title: 第15章 戴夫的告别

content_zh:
维杰里也没提供顺风车，珍妮身上又没通行证，最后只能是打车回到片场，用笑脸骗警卫跟着一起上车，一直跟到摄影棚确认她是演员，又给警卫买了咖啡谢了他的通融，这才顺利赶上午饭后的补妆换衣，理所当然，她错过了午饭，一整个下午都在过度饥饿的眩晕中拍摄。
在拍摄间隙中，珍妮看到切萨雷和吉姆的身影出现在场边，有人过去和他们握手打了招呼，其余的细节，珍妮离的太远，而且一直在工作，所以也无心去留意。她试着去找了下戴夫——她回来以后都还没来得及和他说话，就化妆上戏了。
戴夫也在片场一角，不过离切萨雷他们很远，珍妮也不知道他是否有意为之。在一场接一场谋杀戏码之中，她实在没心思去想这个。
收到一整集剧本以后，演艺空间也就出现了这一集可以选择，只是没有成片观看，也不能选择和华妮塔共情，甚至尼克、华瑞克等人的面目也都很模糊，不过用来配戏已经足够。珍妮已经在演艺空间中试演过好几遍了，算是有过了充足准备，所以虽然下午的戏码也不算是毫无难度，但她多数都是几take就过，很多时候导演多take一遍只是为了换个角度来拍，到时候多点选择余地。
没波没澜地度过了下午的拍摄日程，她的全部戏份就拍摄完毕，之后到正式播出之前，都有可能被召唤过来补拍。CBS剧组会在月内把支票寄给珍妮，结算全部报酬，总之，对珍妮来说，这一次的拍摄可以说是一帆风顺，非但在戏里一切顺利，就是在戏外，也没出现过戴夫担忧的场面，CSI两个花旦角色凯瑟琳和莎拉，同珍妮都没有一对一的对手戏，基本不在一个棚里进行拍摄。
下戏以后，和导演握手寒暄，谢过了他的支持，顺带应下了他某天一起吃饭的邀约，珍妮犹豫了一下，还是先走去找戴夫，她举起手想要和他击掌，“我成功了，戴夫，我的第一次亮相拍完了！”
戴夫也露出微笑，“是的，恭喜你！”
和上午比，他的态度已有了微妙的疏远，珍妮不由皱起眉，她刚想说些什么，吉姆已经走了过来：“嗨，珍妮，恭喜你，你表现得很棒。”
“谢谢你，吉姆。”珍妮对他也热情了不少，不管怎么说，也不论能不能成，吉姆毕竟是把她介绍给了CAA的资深经纪人：“维杰里先生呢？”
“切萨雷两小时前先走了，他还有很多事要处理。”吉姆回答，他又看了戴夫一眼，不过这一次已经没有上午的敌意了，反而带了点同情的意味：“他说他和你晚饭有约？”
“噢，对。”珍妮突然猜到了吉姆为什么会同情戴夫，她马上对戴夫解释说，“我们是要谈合约的事，戴夫，你知道，不是——不是那方面的约会。”
一边说，她一边想起好莱坞之星，“哦！对不起，我得去打个电话，我晚上本来还有工作的，现在得请他们找别人代班了。”
她走到不远处的空地上，拨通了好莱坞之星的电话，一边密切关注吉姆和戴夫，生怕他们又起什么冲突，但出乎意料，两人现在反而还挺友好，吉姆和戴夫聊了一会以后，甚至还拍了拍他的肩膀，而戴夫居然没有挥开，而是还以略带苦涩的笑容。
电话拨通以后，她没心思去观察别人了，而是忙着和老约翰道歉，约翰尼连连叹息，但却没责怪珍妮什么，只是告诉她会扣发昨天的工资，甚至还很有风度地祝福她一切顺利：“不论你要去忙什么，都祝你顺利。”
“谢谢你，老约翰。”珍妮真诚地说，她挂了电话，走到两个男人身边，“现在我要去卸妆和换衣服了，可能还洗个澡——我身上全是玉米糖浆。”
“去吧，”吉姆迅速说，“我会把你送到餐厅的，时间应该正好。”
“戴夫——”珍妮转向戴夫，戴夫对她安抚地一笑，他的情绪看来又好多了。
“我就先回去了。”他说，“下次见，珍妮。”

content_en:
Virgeri didn't provide a ride, and Jenny didn't have a pass. In the end, she had to take a taxi back to the set, use her smile to trick the guard into following her into the car, and followed her to the studio to confirm that she was an actress. She also bought the guard coffee to thank him for his accommodation, and then she was able to make up and change clothes after lunch. Of course, she missed lunch and spent the entire afternoon filming in a dizzy state of excessive hunger.
During the break in filming, Jenny saw Cesare and Jim appearing on the sidelines. Someone went over to shake hands with them and say hello. Jenny was too far away and had been working, so she had no intention of paying attention to the rest of the details. She tried to find Dave - she didn't even have time to talk to him when she came back, before she put on makeup and went on stage.
Dave was also in a corner of the set, but he was far away from Cesare and the others, and Jenny didn't know if he did it intentionally. In the midst of one murder scene after another, she really didn't have the time to think about it.
After receiving the entire episode script, the acting space also showed up with this episode to choose from. However, it was not available to watch as a finished film, nor could one choose to empathize with Warnita. Even the faces of Nick, Warrick, and others were blurred, but it was enough to be used as a supporting role. Jenny has already auditioned several times in the performing arts space, so she is well prepared, so although the afternoon scenes are not without difficulty, she can pass most of them in just a few takes. Many times the director takes more takes just to shoot from a different angle, giving her more choices when the time comes.
The afternoon shooting schedule went through the filming schedule without any trouble, and all her scenes were filmed. From then on, she might be called in for reshoots before the official broadcast. The CBS crew will send a check to Jenny within the month to settle all the remuneration. In short, for Jenny, this filming can be said to be smooth sailing. Not only did everything go smoothly on the set, but also off-screen, there was no scene that Dave was worried about. The two CSI characters Catherine and Sarah did not have one-on-one scenes with Jenny, and they were basically not filmed in the same studio.
After the play, she shook hands with the director, exchanged greetings, thanked him for his support, and accepted his invitation to have dinner together one day. Jenny hesitated for a moment, but went to find Dave first. She raised her hand to give him a high-five, "I succeeded, Dave, my first appearance has been filmed!"
Dave also smiled, "Yes, congratulations!"
Compared with the morning, his attitude was subtly distant. Jenny couldn't help but frown. Just as she was about to say something, Jim had already walked over: "Hi, Jenny, congratulations, you did a great job."
"Thank you, Jim." Jenny was also very enthusiastic towards him. No matter what, regardless of whether it was possible or not, Jim introduced her to CAA's senior agent: "Where's Mr. Vergeri?"
"Cesare left two hours ago. He still has a lot of things to deal with." Jim replied. He looked at Dave again, but this time there was no hostility in the morning, but a bit of sympathy: "He said he had a dinner date with you?"
"Oh, yes." Jenny suddenly guessed why Jim sympathized with Dave, and she immediately explained to Dave, "We are talking about a contract, Dave, you know, not - not a date in that way."
As she spoke, she thought of Hollywood Star, "Oh! Sorry, I have to make a phone call. I had work in the evening, but now I have to ask them to find someone else to take over."
She walked to an open space not far away and dialed the number of Hollywood Star. She paid close attention to Jim and Dave, fearing that they would have another conflict. But unexpectedly, the two were quite friendly now. After Jim and Dave chatted for a while, they even patted him on the shoulder, but Dave actually didn't wave it away, but gave him a slightly bitter smile.
After the call was dialed, she had no intention of observing others. Instead, she was busy apologizing to Old John and making an appointment.Johnny sighed repeatedly, but he didn't blame Jenny for anything. He just told her that yesterday's salary would be withheld. He even wished her all the best in a graceful manner: "No matter what you are going to do, I wish you the best."
"Thank you, John Sr.," Jenny said sincerely. She hung up the phone and walked over to the two men. "Now I'm going to take off my makeup and change my clothes, and maybe take a shower - I'm covered in corn syrup."
"Go ahead," Jim said quickly, "I'll drop you off at the restaurant, it should be just in time."
"Dave—" Jenny turned to Dave, who smiled reassuringly at her. His mood seemed much better again.
"I'll go back first." He said, "See you next time, Jenny."
